1. (Currently amended) A system for providing security in a computer system, the system comprising:
a hardware entropy source including at least one ring oscillator;
one or more logic circuits operatively coupled to the hardware entropy source and configured to:
receive a plurality of independent first entropy values from the hardware entropy source;
apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value;
seed a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;
generate a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and
produce a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number;
wherein the one or more logic circuits include a first logic circuit configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values, a second logic circuit configured to apply the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function, a third logic circuit configured to seed and operate the pseudorandom number generator, and a fourth logic circuit configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code.

2. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the fourth logic circuit being configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes being configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

3. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the fourth logic circuit being configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes being configured to at least:
implement a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

4. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware entropy source comprises at least one ring oscillator configured to generate the plurality of independent first entropy values.

5. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware entropy source is a single hardware source configured to generate the plurality of independent first entropy values.

6. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware entropy source comprises a plurality of independent hardware sources, each configured to generate independent first entropy values that together form the plurality of independent first entropy values.

7. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a permutation function, and the second logic circuit being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.

8. (Currently amended) The system of claim 7, wherein the second logic circuit being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to:
divide the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
apply the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenate the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

9. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a hash function, and the second logic circuit being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function.

10. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and the second logic circuit being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer.

11. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the second logic circuit being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to selectively apply multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

12. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the second logic circuit being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value.

13. (Currently amended) A method of providing security in a computer system, comprising:
receiving a plurality of independent first entropy values from a hardware entropy source including at least one ring oscillator;
applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value;
seeding a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;
generating a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and
producing a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number;
wherein the method includes distinct steps performed by separate logic circuits, including a first logic circuit receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values, a second logic circuit applying the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function, a third logic circuit seeding and operating the pseudorandom number generator, and a fourth logic circuit producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code.

14. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

15. (Original) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes at least:
implementing a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

16. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware entropy source comprises at least one ring oscillator, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the ring oscillator.

17. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware entropy source is a single hardware source, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single hardware source.

18. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware entropy source comprises a plurality of independent hardware sources, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving independent first entropy values from each of the plurality of independent hardware sources.

19. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a permutation function, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 19, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes:
dividing the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
applying the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenating the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

21. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a hash function, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function.

22. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer.

23. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes selectively applying multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

24. (Original) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value.
